title: Closed [e] — é, -er, -ez, -ed, et, les/des/mes (set 2)
sounds: les / des / mes / tes / ses / ces
focus: All of these make the closed [e]: lips spread, tongue high, a pure « ay » with no glide at the end. It's spelled é; -er, -ez and -ed at the end of a word (parler, chez, pied); the word « et »; and the short words les, des, mes, tes, ses, ces. Exceptions: in a few short words the -er is [ɛʁ] with the r pronounced (mer, fer, hiver, cher, hier), and « est » has the open [ɛ]. Québécois keeps é and è clearly apart, even at the end of a word (« parlé » vs « parlait »).

sentences.fr: Aujourd'hui, c'est mon premi[er] jour au c[é]gep.
sentences.en: Today is my first day at CEGEP.

sentences.fr: Je dois trouv[er] l[es] classes [et] rencontr[er] l[es] profs.
sentences.en: I have to find the classrooms and meet the teachers.

sentences.fr: Mon amie H[é]lène m'aide à trouv[er] mon casi[er].
sentences.en: My friend Hélène helps me find my locker.

sentences.fr: « Ass[ez] parl[é] ! » dit le prof. « Ouvr[ez] vos cahi[er]s ! »
sentences.en: "Enough talking!" says the teacher. "Open your notebooks!"

sentences.fr: À midi, je vais dîn[er] avec H[é]lène.
sentences.en: At noon, I'm going to have lunch with Hélène.
